name: second-provider
title: Support Bolt webhooks
body:
## Motivation

We're adding Bolt as a second card processor for EU merchants (PAY-212), and finance wants Bolt payments in the same `payments` table and on the same `payments.<status>` topics as Acme's so reconciliation doesn't need a second pipeline. Bolt's webhooks are simpler than Acme's: one flat JSON shape, a decimal `amount` string, and a base64 HMAC of the body in `x-bolt-signature` with no timestamp.

## Changes

- `WebhookProvider` now has `normalize` next to `verify`, and `secret` is a function so a provider can pick up a rotated secret without a restart. Acme's `normalize` is the identity.
- New `bolt` provider in `loadProviders`: `signBolt` / `verifyBoltSignature` for the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with `BOLT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and `normalizeBolt`, which maps `charge.succeeded` / `charge.failed` / `charge.refunded` onto `payment.succeeded` / `payment.failed` / `refund.created`, `charge_id` onto `paymentId` and the decimal amount onto cents, so Bolt events go through the same `checkWebhookEvent` guard as Acme's.
- `events.payload` now stores the body exactly as the provider sent it (Bolt support asks for the original payload when we open a ticket); dedupe still uses the normalised event's id. Refunds are matched to the payment by `charge_id`, so they don't carry an event id; `ingest` gives an event without one our own id.
- `EventService` applies Bolt charges in their own `applyBolt` method, with the same payment and refund rules as Acme.
- Bolt doesn't send timestamps, so there's no tolerance window to enforce and no replay protection is needed: the `events` UNIQUE constraint already makes a replayed event a no-op.
- Unregistered provider names now fall back to the Acme scheme instead of a 404. Most partners we're talking to are Acme-compatible, so onboarding one becomes a config change rather than a deploy.
- README documents the Bolt payload and both signing schemes.

## Testing

- Unit tests for `verifyBoltSignature` (right secret, wrong secret).
- `app.inject` tests: a signed `charge.succeeded` creates a Bolt payment and a `payments.succeeded` outbox row with the right amount, and a redelivered charge is acknowledged as a duplicate without a second outbox row.
- Sent a few events from Bolt's sandbox to a local server through ngrok and checked them in `/admin/events`.
- Existing Acme tests are unchanged and pass; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are green.

## Open questions

- Bolt events have no `created`, so `normalizeBolt` uses the time we received them. Is that OK for anything downstream that orders by it, or should `created` become optional on `WebhookEvent`?
